newsitem.title: USA: Western Iowa hog movement hit by ice storm-dealers.
newsitem.headline: Western Iowa hog movement hit by ice storm-dealers.

text.p: An ice storm slamming western Iowa, parts of Minnesota and South Dakota has virtually shut off hog marketings in the region on Friday, livestock brokers said.
"We are getting freezing rain and ice-covered highways which is hampering hog movement in the entire southeastern part of south Dakota as well as northwest Iowa," a Sioux Falls livestock broker said.
He noted more snow was forecast for Friday afternoon and early evening. That will pretty much eliminate Saturday kills in Iowa because hogs will not be available, he said.
"We will have limited Saturday kills due to the weather," a St Paul, Minn., broker said.
But weather was milder in eastern Iowa with mostly rain, presenting less of a problem for hog movement.
Livestock dealers in the area hit by the ice storm were mostly quoting hog prices steady to $1.00 per cwt on Friday morning due to short supplies.
